articles.title: 40 years ago June 11, 1986: Army on alert in Haryana | The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Haryana government has alerted the army to meet any situation following a report by the Venkataramiah Commission.  The government also requisitioned about 80 companies of paramilitary forces to help maintain peace. In Cape Town, violence between rival Black groups in a squatter camp resulted in five more deaths, bringing the total to ten. Meanwhile, Sikh extremists in Western Canada planned attacks on Expo-86 with rocket launchers and other weapons.

articles.title: "Erica was described as an emotional asset": Candace Owens keeps pressure on officials over controversial Erika Kirk email - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens doubled down on her Freedom of Information Act request tied to an email mentioning Erika Kirk, claiming federal agencies are resisting her efforts. She accused media personality Andrew Colvett of advising others to lie about the authenticity of the leaked email and alleged that officials prioritized managing public reaction over safety concerns following the shooting incident. Owens argued that the response from government departments only strengthened her suspicions and she remains confident the document is authentic. The dispute surrounding the email's authenticity and the individuals involved continues to fuel online debate.

articles.title: ‘Desperate bid to regain power’: Why Bhagwant Mann is talking about an SAD-BJP reunion | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Bhagwant Mann, Punjab Chief Minister, criticized the possibility of a renewed alliance between the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), arguing it would be opportunistic and detrimental to Punjab.  He stated that such an alliance would not be based on ideology or public welfare, but rather on regaining political power after being rejected by voters. While BJP leaders like Capt Amarinder Singh have expressed support for an alliance, the possibility remains speculative with neither party publicly acknowledging negotiations. The potential alliance is fueled by electoral arithmetic and a desire to regain power in Punjab.

articles.title: Delhi Court Issues Notice To Magistrate Over Bias Allegations In 2 Cases
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi's Principal District and Sessions Judge Vijay Kumar Dahiya has stayed proceedings in two criminal complaint cases pending before a judicial magistrate after the accused persons sought transfer of the matters alleging bias and procedural irregularities. The judge issued notices seeking comments from the magistrate, Komal, and noted that the petitions contained allegations of bias against the presiding officer.  The court will hear the transfer petitions on July 31st.

articles.title: After ascent to CM, Shivakumar’s ties with Bengaluru real estate firms back in focus | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: D K Shivakumar, the new Karnataka Chief Minister, has faced allegations of conflict of interest throughout his political career. These allegations stem from land deals involving real estate firms and projects during his time as urban development minister and involve properties in Benniganahalli, Minerva Mills, and Salarpuria Sattva Divinity project.  Shivakumar's tenure as CM will be scrutinized for its impact on public good versus private profit, particularly given ongoing legal challenges over land ownership disputes and protests against a proposed township in his home district.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of conflict of interest and land deals raise concerns about abuse of power.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu government promoted seven IAS officers without Centre’s approval, Union Ministry tells Madras High Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions stated that the Tamil Nadu government promoted seven Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officers to the grade of Chief Secretary without its approval.  The Madras High Court dismissed a public interest litigation petition challenging this promotion order, stating that only those directly affected by the promotions could file a case. The Union Ministry will take independent action regarding the promotions.

articles.title: EC begins preparations for bypolls to five vacant Assembly seats in T.N. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Archana Patnaik has written to District Collectors seeking details of Returning Officers (ROs) and Assistant Returning Officers (AROs) for the five Assembly seats vacated by members who resigned from the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly. The resignations, following those of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, three AIADMK rebel MLAs, and another rebel MLA, have triggered by-election preparations.  The Election Commission of India (ECI) may announce by-elections within six months.

articles.title: T.N. CM Vijay calls on President, Vice President in New Delhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, visited President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi on Wednesday. He also met with Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan, Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi, and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.  Vijay's visit included discussions with leaders from various political parties, including the Communist Party of India (CPI) and its general secretary D. Raja.

articles.title: Protecting federalism must be the INDIA bloc’s ‘glue’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Omar Abdullah, Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, stated at the June 8, 2026 meeting of the INDIA alliance that the Congress party is uniquely positioned to act as a unifying force due to its presence in all Indian states.  While other parties are limited to specific regions, the Congress's nationwide reach makes it crucial for the alliance's success, according to all participants.  Despite criticisms of the Congress, including concerns about electoral support and potential conflicts with allies, the party is widely recognized as essential for the bloc's advancement.

articles.title: Why TVK is eager to woo AIADMK cadre - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), a new political party formed by defectors from the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK), has been attracting former AIADMK members and officials.  Aadhav Arjuna, a prominent figure in the TVK, stated that it is essentially a "parent body" to the AIADMK. This influx of defectors has led some to question whether the TVK is attempting to strengthen its organizational network by recruiting from the AIADMK.

articles.title: Jawaharlal Nehru was a visionary leader, there can’t be any comparison with Narendra Modi: Sharad Pawar | Mumbai News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Sharad Pawar, NCP (SP) president, stated that there is no comparison between Jawaharlal Nehru and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.  Pawar emphasized the distinct achievements of both leaders during his speech at the party's 27th foundation day celebration in Mumbai. He also highlighted Indira Gandhi's dedication to national interests and condemned the controversial remarks made by Maharashtra BJP minister Girish Mahajan regarding Operation Blue Star, stating that it was a sacrifice for the nation.

articles.title: ‘Gross abuse of law’: Delhi High Court quashes police FIR, ED probe against NewsClick, its founder | Legal News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Sohini Ghosh, a Senior Correspondent for The Indian Express, has moved from Ahmedabad to the New Delhi bureau, focusing on legal developments at the Delhi High Court. Her reporting covers high-profile constitutional disputes, intellectual property issues, criminal and civil cases, human rights concerns, and regulatory law in areas such as technology and healthcare.  Ghosh's previous work included covering crime, law, and policy in Gujarat, including the 2002 riot cases and the 2016 flogging of Dalits in Una. She has also extensively covered health issues in the state.

articles.title: PM Modi credits ‘public maturity’ for NDA’s 12-year stable rule - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised the people for their support and thanked them for allowing him to serve as the longest-serving elected Prime Minister. He highlighted the benefits of a stable government, noting its effectiveness during global crises like the COVID-19 pandemic. Modi emphasized India's progress towards becoming a developed nation, focusing on areas such as renewable energy, self-reliance in sectors like shipping and aviation, and fostering innovation. He called for healthy competition among states to achieve economic growth and technological advancements, while also acknowledging the contributions of youth and women in driving this transformation.

articles.title: Rahul meets Abhishek Banerjee amid push for INDIA bloc coordination - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi met with Abhishek Banerjee, national general secretary of the Trinamool Congress, in New Delhi on Wednesday, June 10, 2026. The meeting followed talks between Mamata Banerjee and Sonia Gandhi earlier that week. These meetings are part of efforts to strengthen unity within the INDIA alliance, which aims to present a united front against the BJP. Congress leadership is also holding internal meetings to discuss current political developments.

articles.title: ‘Judgment indicates what we have always held’, says Newsclick founder after Delhi HC quashes money laundering charges | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Sohini Ghosh, a Senior Correspondent for The Indian Express, has moved from Ahmedabad to the New Delhi bureau, where she focuses on legal developments at the Delhi High Court.  Her reporting covers high-profile constitutional disputes, intellectual property issues, criminal and civil cases, human rights concerns, and regulatory law in areas like technology and healthcare. Previously, Ghosh covered crime, law, and policy in Gujarat, including the 2002 riot cases and the 2016 flogging of Dalits.

articles.title: Fresh hearing ordered on plea seeking FIR against Rahul over remarks on Hindu god Ram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Special Court in Varanasi overturned a Magistrate Court's decision to dismiss an FIR against Rahul Gandhi over alleged remarks about Lord Ram. The court ordered the Magistrate to reconsider the complaint, stating it warranted further review.  The petitioner argued that Gandhi's comments were hate speech and hurt religious sentiments, citing the Supreme Court's recognition of Shri Ram Lalla in its Ram Janmabhoomi judgment and recent disapproval of Gandhi's remarks against V. D. Savarkar.

articles.title: Delhi Gymkhana files: Dead members dining, drone over VIP zone, crores in legal fees, auditor exit | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Gymkhana Club in Delhi is facing scrutiny over alleged misuse of members' cards, high legal expenses, and conflicts of interest.  A draft forensic audit report revealed potential billing irregularities involving deceased members' cards and the club's hiring practices. The club has been criticized for its lack of transparency and control over finances, leading to a refusal by the annual general meeting to approve audited accounts. A drone incident near the Prime Minister's residence in August 2022 also raised security concerns.  The Government-appointed administration continues to withhold a forensic audit report commissioned shortly after taking charge in April 2022.

articles.title: Delhi Confidential: Guess Who? | Delhi Confidential News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Akhilesh Yadav, president of the Samajwadi Party, made a statement during an INDIA bloc meeting that left some Congress leaders uncertain about who he was referring to.  While Akhilesh didn't name anyone, many state unit Congress leaders in UP are opposed to an alliance with the SP. Meanwhile, some BJP leaders in Karnataka have expressed dissatisfaction with Radha Mohan Das Agarwal, the party’s state in-charge. They believe he is inactive and have requested a replacement. The Delhi Police Commissioner Satish Golchha commended his force for preventing a law and order situation during the Cockroach Janta Party's protest rally at Jantar Mantar, Delhi.

articles.title: Donald Trump Is Ready for Fight Night. So Are Donors | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump is hosting a UFC event at the White House on his birthday, marking his present to himself. Sources expect the event to be accompanied by lobbying efforts, as Trump's inner circle anticipates securing support for future initiatives.  The president's administration is also grappling with internal conflicts regarding AI regulation and funding disputes within the Republican party.

articles.title: Delhi Confidential: Guess Who? | Delhi Confidential News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Akhilesh Yadav, president of the Samajwadi Party, made a statement during an INDIA bloc meeting that left some Congress leaders perplexed. He indicated knowledge of Congress members who oppose him, but did not name them. Meanwhile, BJP Karnataka unit leaders are dissatisfied with state in-charge Radha Mohan Das Agarwal, urging the party high command to replace him due to his perceived inactivity.  In contrast, Congress in-charge for Karnataka, Randeep Singh Surjewala, is praised by the party for facilitating a peaceful power transition.

articles.title: Calcutta High Court gives relief to former Minister Aroop Biswas from coercive action in Messi event fiasco - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Calcutta High Court granted interim protection to former Sports Minister and TMC MLA Aroop Biswas against any coercive action in the Lionel Messi event case. Satadru Datta, the organizer of the event, filed an FIR alleging extortion, cheating, and misuse of political influence. The court questioned Biswas's absence for questioning despite two notices from police, ordering him to submit his passport and appear before them after a 48-hour notice. Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya expressed shame over the chaos that unfolded at the event last year, which led to Messi leaving within minutes of arrival.

articles.title: Congress approaches Supreme Court over Meenakshi Natarajan nomination rejection | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress challenged the rejection of its candidate, Meenakshi Natarajan, for the Rajya Sabha election in Madhya Pradesh. The party filed a petition with the Supreme Court after an objection was raised by Rahul Kothari, a BJP state general secretary.  They argued that the returning officer's (RO) order disqualifying Natarajan should be withdrawn as there is no criminal case against her, and she did not have to disclose details of a private complaint in her affidavit. The Congress delegation requested the Election Commission to exercise its constitutional power under Article 324 to intervene and set aside the RO's order.

articles.title: Gujarat Confidential: ‘In-charge’, in line | Ahmedabad News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Gujarat has seen a revolving door of in-charge Directors General of Police (DGP) over the past 13 years.  After several interim appointments, Pramod Kumar served as in-charge DGP for two stints before retiring in March 2018. The state then saw three full-time DGPs: Shivanand Jha, Ashish Bhatia, and Vikas Sahay. All three received extensions to their tenures.

articles.title: Trinamool Congress: "No Trinamool Without Mamata Banerjee": Sagarika Ghose To NDTV
articles.rephrased_article: The Trinamool Congress is facing a severe internal crisis following resignations from senior figures and open rebellion.  MP Sagarika Ghose stated that the party cannot exist without Mamata Banerjee, while criticizing the BJP for weaponizing state agencies to intimidate opposition members. Abhishek Banerjee met with Rahul Gandhi to discuss the INDIA bloc, while Sushmita Dev resigned from the Rajya Sabha and the party, expressing admiration for Himanta Biswa Sarma.  Senior Trinamool figures dismissed speculation of a merger with the Congress.

articles.title: Trump Risks Key Surveillance Authority Over ‘Unqualified’ Spy-Chief Pick | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: A sweeping warrantless surveillance authority, Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, faces a potential lapse in its legal authorization by Friday. President Donald Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence has become a major sticking point in negotiations over reauthorization.  Republican senators, led by John Cornyn, are demanding Pulte's withdrawal before the program can be renewed, while Democrats oppose the move and insist on warrant requirements for American citizens' data. The standoff highlights a broader debate over reforms to Section 702, with some arguing that it is already in effect until March 2027 and others calling for immediate action to address concerns about abuse and transparency.  The House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries has called the situation "deeply dangerous" and urged for a deal that includes warrant requirements.

articles.title: Bill Gates testifies in closed-door US House meeting over Epstein ties | Government News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bill Gates testified in a closed-door session with the House Oversight Committee about his connection to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.  Gates denied any knowledge of Epstein's criminal actions and claimed he never met him beyond a brief meeting in 2011, stating that their interactions were limited and ended in 2014. The committee is investigating Epstein's connections and whether powerful figures may have shielded the financier from accountability.  James Comer, the committee chair, has denied any political motivations behind the investigation and plans to interview other individuals, including investment banker Leon Black, former President Clinton aide Doug Band, and Jes Staley, the former CEO of Barclays.

articles.title: NDA Leaders Adopt Resolution Lauding PM Modi's 12 Years In Power
articles.rephrased_article: The NDA, a coalition of 35 political parties, held a meeting in New Delhi to mark 12 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's continuous service. The meeting, chaired by BJP National President Nitin Nabin, saw the adoption of a resolution recognizing Modi's leadership and contributions to national development. Leaders from across the alliance discussed ways to improve coordination between states and the Centre, focusing on "Ease of Living" and "Ease of Doing Business" reforms under the "Viksit Bharat 2047" vision.  PM Modi thanked the leaders for their support and reaffirmed the NDA's commitment to serving the nation.

articles.title: Meenakshi Natarajan nomination: Congress leaders eyeing RS seat ‘spoilt’ chances of party nominee, says M.P. CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Mohan Yadav of Madhya Pradesh accused the Congress of deliberately sabotaging Meenakshi Natarajan's nomination for a Rajya Sabha seat, alleging that it was part of an attempt to secure the seat themselves.  The nomination was rejected by the Returning Officer based on allegations of undisclosed information in her form, which led to Mahesh Kewat, the BJP candidate for the third seat, winning unopposed. The Congress has challenged the rejection and plans a statewide protest.

articles.title: Trump directs interim US intelligence chief Bill Pulte to downsize agency | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump directed Bill Pulte, a businessman with no intelligence background, to downsize the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) as soon as he takes up his interim role on June 19th.  Democrats have criticized Pulte's appointment, questioning his qualifications and seeing him as a Trump loyalist who has attacked his critics. Mark Warner, a key figure on the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, called Pulte "grossly unqualified" and warned that his appointment would complicate negotiations to renew Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA).  Trump has defended Pulte's appointment and called for Congress to pass a temporary extension of Section 702.

articles.title: "Morally Wrong": Rebel's "I Miss You Didi" Message For Mamata Banerjee
articles.rephrased_article: Satabdi Roy, a Trinamool Congress rebel MP, and Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, the party's rebel 'Chief Whip', have written to Speaker Om Birla expressing support for the NDA.  Roy, who was brought into politics by Mamata Banerjee, feels politically right but morally conflicted about her decision. She believes corruption within the party alienated voters and that Banerjee's refusal to address it led to the party's defeat. Roy also expressed concern over Banerjee's leadership and suggested a potential merger with the Congress, while acknowledging her emotional attachment to the former chief minister.

articles.title: Ex AIADMK Minister P Benjamin, Supporters Join DMK
articles.rephrased_article: P Benjamin, former AIADMK minister, joined the DMK on Wednesday in the presence of party president M K Stalin and senior leaders.  Benjamin was accompanied by several AIADMK office-bearers, including Tiruvallur Central Party District Women's Wing secretary Yamini Ilayaraja and scores of other officials.  MK Stalin welcomed Benjamin and his supporters to the DMK on social media.

articles.title: "Great PM, Wise Man": Trump Congratulates PM Modi On Completing 12 Years
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump congratulated Narendra Modi on becoming India's longest-serving prime minister, calling him a "great" leader and a "strong, healthy, and wise man."  Modi surpassed Jawaharlal Nehru's record of 4,398 days in office. Other world leaders who congratulated Modi included Benjamin Netanyahu, Giorgia Meloni, Dmitry Peskov, Ursula von der Leyen, Friedrich Merz, Mark Carney, and Rishi Sunak.

articles.title: After a Democrat standoff, Trump signs $70bn immigration enforcement bill | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump signed a $70 billion immigration enforcement bill into law, despite ongoing criticism from Democrats who oppose the funding. The legislation provides additional resources for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Patrol (CBP), which fall under the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).  The bill was passed after a months-long standoff over the funding, with Republicans ultimately securing enough votes to override Democrats' objections. The legislation has drawn condemnation from immigrant rights groups who fear it will lead to increased deportations and violence against immigrants.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay Meets Sonia, Rahul Gandhi In Delhi
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay met with Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi in New Delhi on Wednesday.  Vijay is attending the Niti Aayog governing council meeting on Thursday, marking his second visit to the capital since becoming chief minister in May. The meeting was a courtesy call, with the Gandhis wishing Vijay well for his future as chief minister.

articles.title: Three questions Bill Gates could face as he testifies to Congress on Epstein
articles.rephrased_article: Bill Gates, co-founder of Microsoft and philanthropist, testified before a congressional committee about his past association with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The committee is questioning Gates on why he continued to meet with Epstein despite knowing about his criminal history, the lack of transparency in their relationship, and whether Epstein sought to influence Gates or blackmail him.  The committee also wants to know if Gates's foundation was ever influenced by Epstein's claims that he could secure philanthropic funding.

articles.title: Former AIADMK Minister P. Benjamin joins DMK - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P. Benjamin, a former AIADMK minister, joined the DMK on Wednesday in Chennai. M.K. Stalin, the party president, welcomed him to the organization.  Benjamin previously served as the Deputy Mayor of Chennai Corporation and held ministerial positions in the education and rural industries sectors. He contested for the Maduravoyal constituency in the 2026 Assembly election but lost. Benjamin stated his intention to continue serving the public after joining the DMK.

articles.title: Second Trinamool MP quits Rajya Sabha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sushmita Dev, a Trinamool Congress MP, resigned from the Rajya Sabha and the party on Wednesday (June 10, 2026), citing her inability to fulfill the expectations of her constituents in Assam. Dev met with Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma shortly after her resignation, but did not confirm if it was a step towards joining the BJP.  This follows another MP's resignation from the party this week and speculation about ownership of the Trinamool Congress in the Lok Sabha.

articles.title: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray distances himself from TMC rebel group - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray, former TMC Chief Whip in the Rajya Sabha, resigned from his Upper House seat on Monday and praised colleagues who rebelled against Mamata Banerjee and her nephew, Abhishek Banerjee.  He clarified that he was unaware of a meeting with other rebels at actor-turned-politician Shatabdi Roy's residence before joining them for 30-40 minutes. Ray also stated his support for the rebellion but did not attend the meeting. He expressed hope for the new BJP government in West Bengal and acknowledged past harassment he faced within the TMC, prompting him to consider leaving politics altogether.

articles.title: Majority of workers with NCP(SP) official faction, claim leaders - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P.M. Suresh Babu, the new NCP(SP) State president, stated that a majority of party workers in Kerala remain loyal to the central leadership despite a split within the organization.  He refuted claims by a rival faction led by former Minister A.K. Saseendran and Thomas K. Thomas, stating that these allegations are baseless as Supriya Sule, the working president, attended the INDIA bloc meeting in New Delhi.  Babu asserted that the Kerala unit will stand firm with the Left front and reject attempts to induct the rival faction into the front.

articles.title: 'No Merger With Congress': Trinamool Rebel Leader Ritabrata Banerjee Claims Support Of 64 MLAs
articles.rephrased_article: Ritabrata Banerjee, leader of a rebel faction within the Trinamool Congress (TMC), denies any merger plans with the Congress party. He claims his camp now supports 64 MLAs who are preparing to formally submit a letter to the Assembly Speaker.  Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury, a senior Congress leader, denies knowledge of any such talks. Meanwhile, Sushmita Dev, a Rajya Sabha MP and former TMC member, has resigned from both positions and plans to work in Assam. The rebel faction is seeking separate seating arrangements and meeting with BJP leaders, sparking speculation about potential merger with the NDA.

articles.title: Meenakshi Natarajan Row And Congress' Article 324 Demand. What It Is
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leader Meenakshi Natarajan's Rajya Sabha nomination was rejected for nondisclosure of a pending court case. The party is urging the Election Commission (EC) to use its powers under Article 324 to overturn the Returning Officer's decision, arguing that the alleged omission does not warrant disqualification.  The EC has the power to oversee elections and ensure free and fair processes, but experts question whether this provision can override specific legal provisions or be used as a substitute for existing remedies like Election Petitions. The EC is currently examining the Congress' representation and seeking the Returning Officer's report before making a decision.

articles.title: Rajasthan Congress: After Ashok Gehlot's Outburst, Sachin Pilot's Message On "Restraint"
articles.rephrased_article: Sachin Pilot, former Rajasthan Chief Minister, emphasized patience, restraint, and humility in politics at a Karauli farmers' conference. He recalled his father's courage against godman Chandraswami's influence in the 1990s and stressed that public life should be guided by truth, principles, and courage. Ashok Gehlot, former Rajasthan Chief Minister, had previously made statements about Pilot and the September 2022 showdown, which did not allow a change of guard in the state. Ramesh Meena, former Congress minister, criticized Gehlot's allegations against MLAs who sided with Pilot, calling for a narco-analysis test to expose the truth.

articles.title: What are Lebanon’s most important political parties? | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Hezbollah, a powerful Shia Muslim party, has been a key player in Lebanese politics since its formation during the Lebanese Civil War. It is funded by Iran and maintains close ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The Lebanese Forces (LF), a right-wing Christian party, are currently the largest Christian party in parliament.  Amal Movement, another Shia Muslim party allied with Hezbollah, has been led by Nabih Berri since 1980 and is known for its militia operations. Future Movement, founded by Rafik Hariri, is now predominantly Sunni and was once a prominent pro-West bloc. The Free Patriotic Movement (FPM), founded by Michel Aoun, is a Christian party that has lost some of its influence in recent years.  The Progressive Socialist Movement is a Druze party with a history of involvement in the Lebanese Civil War.

articles.title: At NDA Meet On Completing 12 Years, PM Narendra Modi's 'Congress Growth Rate' Jab
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted his government's achievements during 12 years in office, emphasizing the end of Congress dominance and a shift to rapid development. He attributed the growth to the NDA rule, contrasting it with the "Congress Growth Rate" characterized by stagnation and lack of progress. Modi also praised his government's actions on issues like Article 370 abolition, Northeast peace restoration, counter-terrorism operations, and social reforms. The BJP passed a resolution praising Modi's leadership and vowing to continue people-centric development.

articles.title: Cabinet passes resolution praising PM Modi’s tenure record - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Cabinet congratulated Narendra Modi on becoming the longest-serving elected Prime Minister of India, surpassing former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru's record. The Cabinet adopted resolutions praising his leadership in poverty alleviation, inclusive growth, and national security, highlighting achievements like strengthening the economy and expanding manufacturing capabilities.  The resolution also acknowledged the country's progress in areas such as women empowerment, scientific advancement, and global engagement.

articles.title: EC acted as per law in Meenakshi Natarajan case, says Telangana BJP chief - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Ramchander Rao, Telangana BJP president, defended the Election Commission's disqualification of Congress Party candidate Meenakshi Natarajan, stating she failed to disclose a pending case in her affidavit. He argued that candidates are required to disclose all pending cases and assets and cited precedent for unseating an MLA for similar reasons.  Rao also addressed various issues including the NEET question paper leak, CBSE evaluation issues, Ayushman Bharat Health Insurance card usage, inter-state matters with Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, and Prime Minister Modi's press conference style.

articles.title: BJP Marks PM Narendra Modi's Record 12-Year Tenure With Pujas, Aartis Across Delhi
articles.rephrased_article: BJP leaders and Union ministers held prayers across Delhi, marking the occasion of Narendra Modi becoming India's longest-serving elected Prime Minister.  The celebrations coincided with Modi surpassing Jawaharlal Nehru's record of 4,399 days in office.  Rekha Gupta, Chief Minister of Delhi, praised Modi's leadership and highlighted the achievements of his government over the past twelve years. Union Ministers J.P. Nadda, Ashwini Vaishnaw, and Om Birla also offered prayers and lauded Modi's governance. The celebrations were met with criticism from the opposition, who accused Modi of celebrating a "self-proclaimed" achievement.

articles.title: EC acted as per law in Meenakshi Natarajan case, says Telangana BJP chief - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Ramchander Rao, Telangana BJP president, defended the Election Commission’s disqualification of Congress Party Rajya Sabha candidate Meenakshi Natarajan for failing to disclose a pending case in her affidavit. He argued that candidates are obligated to disclose all pending cases and assets, citing precedent and emphasizing that the Election Commission acted according to established procedures. Rao also addressed various other issues, including alleged conspiracies behind NEET question paper leaks and CBSE evaluation problems, as well as calls for expanding Ayushman Bharat Health Insurance coverage.

articles.title: 12 Years Of 'Decolonisation': How Modi Government Shed British-Era Practices
articles.rephrased_article: The Narendra Modi government has undertaken a significant effort to dismantle symbols and practices associated with British colonial rule over the past twelve years. This includes renaming landmarks like Rajpath to Kartavya Path, incorporating Indian motifs in new buildings like the Parliament building, and replacing outdated laws with new ones.  The government has also renamed three islands in the Andaman and Nicobar chain and changed several other aspects of public life, including street names, office titles, and even the budget presentation date. These changes reflect a broader effort to reclaim India's identity and culture.

articles.title: Waste Management Scam In Karnataka? BJP Alleges Rs 10,000-Crore Kickback
articles.rephrased_article: R Ashok, Leader of the Opposition in Karnataka, alleged a massive Rs 39,000-crore scam in the city's waste processing system. He claimed that the new contract awarded to MSW Solutions Limited, linked to Ramky Group, involves kickbacks worth Rs 10,000 crore and raises waste processing costs from Rs 6,117 crore to Rs 39,437 crore over a 35-year period. Ashok also alleged procedural violations in the tender process, including inadequate scrutiny and failure to publish mandatory advertisements. He demanded an immediate cancellation of the contract and urged Governor Thawar Chand Gehlot to order a probe into the matter.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of a massive financial scam involving public funds raise serious concerns.

articles.title: Madhya Pradesh Removes Two-Child Norm For Government Employees
articles.rephrased_article: Madhya Pradesh's government has reversed its two-child restriction policy for government servants.  Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav ordered the removal of the provision from the state's Civil Services Rules, which had barred candidates with more than two living children from government jobs since 2001. The decision aligns the state with Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh, which have also lifted similar restrictions. This move is expected to provide relief for job aspirants and government employees who previously faced this policy.

articles.title: MS Aiyar Wasn't Joking: How His Old 'Football' Theory Explains Trinamool's Implosion
articles.rephrased_article: The Trinamool Congress (TMC) is experiencing a significant internal crisis following its electoral defeat in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections. The party's decline, marked by rebel MPs and dwindling attendance at meetings, suggests an inability to adapt to post-power dynamics.  Mamata Banerjee faces difficult choices: fighting legal battles, seeking reconciliation with rebels, rebuilding from the grassroots, or forming a larger anti-BJP alliance. However, these options present their own challenges, including potential power struggles and ideological conflicts. The party's future hinges on whether it can regain its former strength and identity as a political force in Bengal.

articles.title: Rajya Sabha polls: Congress delegation meets ECI over rejection of Meenakshi Natarajan’s nomination - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Congress delegation, including general secretary K.C. Venugopal and candidate Meenakshi Natarajan, met with the Election Commission of India (ECI) on Wednesday to address the rejection of her nomination for Rajya Sabha polls in Madhya Pradesh.  Mr. Singhvi, a member of the delegation, argued that the court notice was based on a private complaint and not a criminal case, and requested the commission to withdraw the order of rejection. The party president Mallikarjun Kharge convened an urgent meeting for Congress leaders to discuss the situation.

articles.title: Graham Platner wins Maine primary election: Results and key takeaways | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Graham Platner won the Maine Democratic primary for US Senate, defeating Susan Collins.  He will face off against the incumbent in November. In South Carolina, Nancy Mace lost her bid for re-election after losing to Pamela Evette, who is expected to win the general election.  In Nevada, Marty O’Donnell won the Republican primary for the 3rd Congressional District.   The results of these primaries signal a potential shift in power dynamics in Congress and the Senate.

articles.title: Rajya Sabha polls: Congress delegation meets ECI over rejection of Meenakshi Natarajan’s nomination - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Congress delegation, including general secretary K.C. Venugopal and candidate Meenakshi Natarajan, met with the Election Commission of India (ECI) on Wednesday to address the rejection of Natarajan's nomination for Rajya Sabha polls in Madhya Pradesh.  The delegation argued that the court notice was based on a private complaint, not a criminal case, and requested the commission to withdraw the rejection order. The party president, Mallikarjun Kharge, convened an urgent meeting to discuss the situation.

articles.title: Not a single rupee from the State: Jagan demands ₹1 crore each for steel blast families - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, former Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh and president of the YSR Congress Party, visited Visakhapatnam to console families of workers injured in a recent blast at the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (VSP).  He accused the NDA government of failing to protect the plant from privatization and neglecting the welfare of its employees.  The VSP workforce has been reduced from 28,000 to approximately 16,000 over the past two years, according to Jagan.

articles.title: Trinamool Congress Mamata Banerjee: 'Offer Has To Come From Trinamool': Congress Sources Amid Merger Buzz
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, national general secretary of the Trinamool Congress, met with Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition, for one and a half hours on Wednesday to strengthen coordination within the opposition INDIA bloc. The meeting followed Mamata Banerjee's meeting with Sonia Gandhi, where they discussed the need for greater unity against the BJP.  The Trinamool Congress conveyed its desire for a strong alliance and accepted Rahul Gandhi's leadership, while Congress has made it clear that any merger proposal must come from them. This comes amidst internal rebellion within the Trinamool Congress, with some MLAs and MPs considering an alliance with the BJP.

articles.title: Inside the Prime Minister Modi's Vision for a Global Bharat
articles.rephrased_article: Narendra Modi, the longest-serving continuously elected Prime Minister of India, has been praised for his thought leadership. His emphasis on drawing inspiration from India's civilisational past to address contemporary challenges and shape aspirations for a great future is evident in his policies.  He promotes "Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi" by renaming public places and buildings, celebrating national occasions like International Yoga Day, and emphasizing education in the mother tongue. Modi's leadership has also been marked by his focus on empowering citizens through participation in development, promoting gender justice, and addressing environmental challenges with practical solutions. His ideas have inspired a collective national aspiration for "Vikas" or progress.

articles.title: Congress calls Returning Officer’s order on Meenakshi Natarajan’s Rajya Sabha nomination ‘egregious’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress officials, including general secretary K.C. Venugopal and senior leader Abhishek Manu Singhvi, met with the Election Commission of India (ECI) on Wednesday to appeal against the rejection of their Madhya Pradesh Rajya Sabha candidate Meenakshi Natarajan's nomination. The delegation argued that the Returning Officer's decision was "egregious, blatantly unlawful" and detrimental to democracy. They emphasized that the order violated provisions of the Representation of the People Act and urged the Commission to reverse its decision before the withdrawal deadline.  The Congress leaders stressed the importance of preserving a level-playing field in elections and warned that failing to intervene could create a skewed system.

articles.title: Mocked online, tested in ministry: As Hyundai bets on Tamil Nadu, Keerthana has last laugh | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: S Keerthana, Tamil Nadu's 29-year-old Industries Minister, visited the HD Hyundai Heavy Industries shipyard in South Korea as part of her efforts to reassure investors and demonstrate continuity with previous industrial commitments.  The visit was seen as a response to online criticism and mockery she has faced since taking office, with some questioning whether she would embrace or distance herself from projects associated with the previous DMK government. Keerthana, who entered politics through campaign work rather than traditional party hierarchies, is navigating her role in a political landscape dominated by men who ascended through established party structures.  Her unconventional path and lack of conventional political baggage may be an advantage as she faces challenges in managing complex industrial projects.

articles.title: West Bengal TMC Crisis Live Update, Mamata Banerjee: Sushmita Dev On Quitting Trinamool: Long Story, Won't Comment On Mamata Didi
articles.rephrased_article: Sushmita Dev, a former Congress leader and Trinamool Congress MP, resigned from the Rajya Sabha, citing personal reasons. She is the second Trinamool MP to resign this week following Sukhendu Sekhar Ray.  Dev's resignation follows her meeting with Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and her decision to support the BJP-led NDA government. The rebellion within the party has led to concerns about a potential split, potentially bringing the NDA closer to its two-thirds majority goal in the Lok Sabha.

articles.title: Sushmita Dev Quits Trinamool, Meets Himanta Biswa Sarma For "Guidance"
articles.rephrased_article: Sushmita Dev, a Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha MP, resigned from all party posts and her membership on Wednesday.  She cited personal reasons for her decision, stating she wants to focus on serving the people of Assam. This follows the resignation of another Trinamool Rajya Sabha member, Sukhendu Sekhar Ray, who also criticized the party's leadership in a press statement. Dev joined the Trinamool in 2021 after previously serving as an MP from Silchar in Assam.

articles.title: ‘The party stands united’: Sanjay Raut dismisses rumours of 7 Sena (UBT) MPs defecting to Shinde camp | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Sanjay Raut, spokesperson for the Shiv Sena (UBT), denied reports that seven of its nine Lok Sabha MPs are planning to defect. He stated that the party remains united and that those who have previously defected will eventually do so.  Raut also condemned the trend of political defections, blaming central institutions and investigative agencies for creating an environment that incentivizes them. While acknowledging communication between factions, he emphasized that these conversations do not indicate defection.

articles.title: Ahead of Karnataka SIR, Congress seeks printed copies of 2002 electoral rolls from EC | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) has requested the Election Commission of India (ECI) for printed copies of 2002 electoral rolls and related documents ahead of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. The request was made by Ramesh Babu, MLC and Chairman of the KPCC Media and Communication Department, who cited the need for comparative verification and effective participation in the SIR process.  The party aims to identify discrepancies and ensure accurate voter registration.

articles.title: Kerala government considering comprehensive prison reforms: Ramesh Chennithala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala announced plans to overhaul Kerala's prison system, including potentially adding a new central prison due to overcrowding.  He also emphasized the need for increased staff and strengthened production units within prisons. The discussion focused on initiatives like chapatti manufacturing and petrol pumps that generate revenue for prison development. Chennithala extended the inquiry into prisoner escapes during the previous LDF government's tenure, while stating prisoners would not be granted parole based solely on political grounds.

articles.title: Awami members can fight local polls as independents - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Tarique Rahman-led government has announced that party members will be allowed to contest the upcoming local government elections in their individual capacities. PM Zahed Ur Rahman clarified that individuals holding party positions would be eligible, but using banned organization names or slogans during campaigning would be prohibited. The move comes amidst a resurgence of Awami League supporters and street processions despite its ban under anti-terrorism laws.  The government is expected to begin the phased rollout of local elections after the monsoon season, likely starting in September or October.

articles.title: How do you intend to appoint Director of Prosecution? Madras High Court asks T.N. Govt - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court granted a two-week extension to the Tamil Nadu government to provide details on its appointment procedures for Director, Deputy Director, and Assistant Director positions in the Prosecution department. The court's decision followed a writ petition filed by five Additional and Assistant Public Prosecutors who challenged Section 20 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), arguing that it allows appointments to these posts without prior experience as public prosecutors.  The petitioners also sought statutory rules for future appointments and an injunction against appointing individuals outside the regular cadre of prosecuting officers.

articles.title: Jan Dhan Yojana To Ayushman Bharat: 5 Schemes That Marked PM Narendra Modi's 12 Years
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has served as India's longest continuously serving PM for 12 years, overseeing a series of government schemes that have significantly impacted the lives of millions.  These include the Swachh Bharat Mission, which built over 12 crore toilets and declared 753 districts Open Defecation Free, and the Ayushman Bharat program, providing free healthcare to over 44 crore people with 10 crore hospital admissions. Other notable schemes include the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), which aims to provide financial inclusion for unbanked adults, and the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY), which provides affordable housing for urban and rural poor.  These initiatives have transformed India's social and economic landscape.

articles.title: Congress tries moving MLAs to Karnataka – in vain – as Meenakshi Natarajan’s Rajya Sabha nomination is rejected | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP secured a victory in the Rajya Sabha election after rejecting the nomination of Congress leader Meenakshi Natarajan. The rejection came after the BJP challenged her nomination, alleging incomplete disclosure of information related to a court case.  Despite attempts by the Congress to move its legislators to Karnataka to avoid potential influence from the BJP, the decision was made and the party's candidate was ultimately rejected. The BJP celebrated the victory while the Congress condemned the decision as an attempt to undermine democracy.

articles.title: Frequent disruptions in legislatures pose a serious challenge to democratic institutions: Om Birla - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Om Birla, Speaker of the Lok Sabha, emphasized that frequent disruptions in legislative institutions pose a challenge to democratic principles. He urged state and central legislatures to promote conduct aligned with public expectations and meaningful discussion. The second conference of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) India Region Zone-II (North Zone) concluded with four resolutions aimed at making legislative institutions more effective, accountable, and people-centric.  These resolutions are expected to contribute to the progress of parliamentary and democratic institutions in India.

articles.title: Vijay to attend NITI Aayog Governing Council meeting in Delhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister, will attend the 11th Governing Council meeting of NITI Aayog in New Delhi on Thursday.  He is scheduled to meet with political leaders in New Delhi before participating in the council meeting alongside other state and UT chief ministers and lieutenant governors. This marks his second visit to the national capital since becoming Chief Minister.

articles.title: Stand-off over Bengaluru Development portfolio likely to be discussed in Delhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Krishna Byre Gowda, Karnataka's Minister for Bengaluru Development, is reportedly dissatisfied with the truncated portfolio he received.  He has expressed his discontent to Congress Central leadership, amidst a critical monsoon season and an absence of elected councillors in Bengaluru due to delayed elections for five corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA).

articles.title: Do not want confrontation with Governor, but cannot compromise on State’s rights, says Tamil Nadu Higher Education Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan stated that the government would not compromise on its autonomy in appointing Vice-Chancellors of state universities, despite a potential confrontation with Governor. He emphasized the importance of cooperation between the Governor and the Chief Minister for the smooth functioning of universities, drawing an analogy to the need for equal size wheels on a vehicle.

articles.title: Issue certified copies of Udhayanidhi Stalin’s nomination papers to defeated candidate, Madras High Court directs ECI - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court ordered the Chennai district election officer to provide certified copies of Udhayanidhi Stalin's accepted and rejected nomination papers and affidavits. The order came after a writ petition filed by P. Milany, who lost the Chepauk-Thiruvallikeni constituency election to Mr. Udhayanidhi Stalin, was allowed.  The court granted this request before the results were officially declared on May 4th, 2026.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker J.C.D. Prabhakar’s decision marks a throwback to the experience of 11 AIADMK MLAs in 2017-18 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: J.C.D. Prabhakar, the Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker, has chosen not to pursue disqualification proceedings against 21 AIADMK legislators, a decision reminiscent of an eight-year-old incident where 11 MLAs faced similar scrutiny but were spared by then-Speaker P. Dhanapal.  Unlike that instance, no formal announcement was made and the matter ultimately went to the Madras High Court, which dismissed a plea for action against the legislators.

articles.title: Rebel TMC MPs siding with BJP, says Kalyan Banerjee - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following a rebellion by 20 Trinamool Congress Lok Sabha members, loyalists of Mamata Banerjee held a press conference in New Delhi, accusing the rebel MPs of siding with the Bharatiya Janata Party.  Kalyan Banerjee, Chief Whip of the party in the Lok Sabha, and Kirti Azad addressed the media, questioning the authenticity of the letter by the rebels stating they were creating a separate bloc within the Trinamool Congress to support the BJP-led NDA government. They also criticized the rebel MPs for lacking political morality and abandoning party workers.  Several loyalists of Mamata Banerjee expressed their disapproval of the CID search at her residence, questioning its purpose and accusing the rebels of targeting party leaders with the help of the BJP.

articles.title: Congress, Sena (UBT) seek Girish Mahajan’s removal over Operation Blue Star remarks | Mumbai News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders demanded the removal of Maharashtra minister Girish Mahajan from his cabinet position, accusing him of undermining the armed forces.  They criticized Mahajan's comments on Operation Blue Star, calling them a betrayal of national interests and questioning India’s fight against terrorism. Harshvardhan Sapkal, Maharashtra Congress president, called for Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis to publicly condemn Mahajan's remarks.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article discusses potentially inflammatory remarks about a sensitive historical event.

articles.title: Modi will surpass Nehru’s record to become longest serving PM of India: Amit Shah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Amit Shah, Union Home Minister, announced that Prime Minister Narendra Modi will surpass former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru's record for the longest continuous term as an elected Indian Prime Minister.  On Wednesday, June 10th, members of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) will meet to mark 12 years of their rule.  Shah launched the Land Port Management System (LPMS) on Tuesday, June 9th, emphasizing its role in border security and facilitating trade. The system aims to create a secure and modern border management framework by streamlining processes and enhancing coordination among agencies.

articles.title: Amid CID searches and TMC rebellion, Mamata meets Sonia in Delhi | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee met with Sonia Gandhi in Delhi to discuss coordination among the INDIA bloc parties.  The West Bengal CID conducted searches at the Trinamool Congress’s central party office and the office of its national general secretary, Abhishek Banerjee, as part of an investigation into alleged Assembly signature forgery. The TMC leader, Kalyan Banerjee, stated that the party is not worried about rebel MPs joining the NDA and maintains that their strength lies in "Maa, Maati and Maanush".

articles.title: TVK government comes under fire for blocking channels on Arasu Cable TV - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Edappadi K. Palaniswami, general secretary of the AIADMK, complained that telecasts from three Tamil television channels, Polimer News, News Tamil TV 24X7, and Tamil Janam News, were blocked on the platform of Arasu Cable TV. He cited a similar incident involving Puthiya Thalaimurai a few weeks prior, where protests by the Opposition led to its reinstatement. Palaniswami questioned whether there was an oversight body monitoring electronic media and social media content.

articles.title: Meenakshi Natarajan named as respondent in private complaint - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders in Telangana are investigating the rejection of Meenakshi Natarajan, the party's in-charge for the state, for her Rajya Sabha nomination papers. The rejection stems from a private petition filed by a former Congress leader and ex-Municipal Corporator in 2025.  The document was submitted to the Court of the 4th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate at Hyderabad.

articles.title: Gujarat, a State without an Opposition - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shaktisinh Gohil, the Congress leader whose term in the Rajya Sabha ends on June 21, will be the first representative from Gujarat's opposition to leave the Upper House since the state's formation in 1960. This vacancy is a product of electoral arithmetic and reflects the BJP's sustained dominance in Gujarat since 1995, which has resulted in an overwhelming majority in the State Assembly and consequently determined Rajya Sabha representation.

articles.title: Trinamool Congress Crisis, Trinamool: "She Said Will Fight, Rebuild": Kirti Azad On Mamata Banerjee's Crisis Plan
articles.rephrased_article: Kirti Azad, a Trinamool Congress MP, criticized rebel MPs who he called "traitors" and accused them of seeking power. He alleged that these individuals were being blackmailed and threatened with coercion to join the BJP. Mamata Banerjee, the party's chief, has vowed to rebuild the party and fight again on the streets. Azad also claimed that several rebels, including Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, had been caught taking bribes and that they lacked loyalty to the party. He asserted that these individuals would not be able to win in future elections.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of blackmail and coercion within a political party raise serious concerns.

articles.title: Will Hobnobbing With Trinamool Rebels Cost BJP? What State Leaders Say
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, the West Bengal Chief Minister, met with rebel Trinamool Congress MPs at Satabdi Roy's Delhi residence. This meeting followed a similar gathering of the rebels at Bhupendra Yadav's home earlier in the day. Despite these meetings, the BJP maintains it will not induct any Trinamool leaders into its ranks. The BJP leadership argues that this gesture is a political move to weaken the Trinamool party and prepare for upcoming elections.  The BJP has stated that they are focused on cleaning Bengal of the Trinamool party.

articles.title: NDA Constituents To Meet Tomorrow For 12th Anniversary Of Modi Government
articles.rephrased_article: A meeting of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) will be held on Wednesday to celebrate 12 years of the government's rule and Prime Minister Narendra Modi becoming the longest continuously serving elected prime minister of India. The event, attended by all constituents of the ruling alliance besides top BJP leadership, including Prime Minister Modi, is expected to see a resolution praising his record.  Senior Union ministers like Rajnath Singh, Amit Shah, J P Nadda, and Shivraj Singh Chouhan are among those expected to attend.  The meeting will focus on boosting 'Ease of Living', 'Ease of Doing Business', and reforms towards realizing the shared dream of a 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047.

articles.title: 'Not Done By Us': Surat Civic Body Distances Itself From Nasirnagar Demolition
articles.rephrased_article: The Surat Municipal Corporation (SMC) has denied any involvement in the demolition of homes in Nasirnagar, Surat.  Ashish J Nayak, Deputy Commissioner of the SMC, stated that his team was only there for boundary demarcation and that machinery was already operating when they arrived. He also clarified that the police and SOG were not summoned by the SMC and that the standard procedure for demolition notices is followed, which includes providing residents with advance notice. The state government is investigating the incident to determine who authorized the demolition.

articles.title: Congress, Trinamool Congress: After Hug At INDIA Huddle, A Mamata Banerjee-Sonia Gandhi Meet At 10 Janpath
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, leader of the Trinamool Congress, met with Sonia Gandhi, chairperson of the Congress Parliamentary Party, at her residence in Delhi. The meeting followed a recent photo of their embrace at an INDIA bloc meeting and comes amid significant challenges for both parties, including rebellions within their ranks.  Experts suggest that no major discussions took place without Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition, present.

articles.title: Meenakshi Natarajan's Nomination Scrapped, Congress Explores Legal Options
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders protested outside the Election Commission headquarters in Delhi after the rejection of their Rajya Sabha candidate, Meenakshi Natarajan,'s nomination papers.  The Election Commission acknowledged the Congress memorandum and is expected to seek a report from the Returning Officer over the controversy. Senior Congress leaders, including KC Venugopal, Jairam Ramesh, Sachin Pilot, and Bhupesh Baghel, staged a protest, while sources say the party is preparing for a legal challenge against the rejection.

articles.title: Bengal government to remove ‘Dham’ tag from name of Digha temple - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The West Bengal government, led by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, will remove the word “Dham” from the name of the Jagannath temple in Digha. The decision was prompted by a letter from Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and follows objections from the state BJP leadership and religious authorities who argued that the term "Dham" is exclusive to the four sacred sites in Hinduism.  The government will maintain the temple's cultural center complex, but remove the word “Dham” from its name.

articles.title: Bengal BJP govt’s first month: From anti-corruption drive, border fencing to new welfare schemes | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The newly formed BJP government in West Bengal has taken several significant steps in its first month, including transferring land to the Border Security Force for border fencing and expanding the state's flagship subsidized food program.  The government has also launched an anti-corruption drive, arresting over 300 TMC leaders accused of corruption. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has promised to tackle issues like illegal infiltration and address concerns about welfare schemes. However, the government has faced criticism for its "bulldozer culture" approach to evicting street hawkers without proper rehabilitation.  The BJP government is still in its early stages and faces a long road ahead.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Mass arrests without due process raise concerns about abuse of power.

articles.title: Meat shops out of Varanasi? New civic body plan has traders and Opposition up in arms | Lucknow News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Varanasi Municipal Corporation has proposed relocating meat, fish, and poultry shops to the city's outskirts, citing hygiene concerns and preservation of religious character. The proposal, approved by the executive committee and municipal corporation, aims to create designated markets with proper facilities. However, the move has sparked criticism from opposition parties and traders who argue that it will negatively impact livelihoods and inconvenience consumers.  The Samajwadi Party and UP Congress have questioned the selective action against meat shops while liquor outlets remain untouched. Traders have expressed concerns about accessibility, customer convenience, and economic losses associated with relocating their businesses. They propose alternative solutions like enclosed modern outlets or restrictions around temple areas instead of full relocation.
articles.civic_flag_reason: It potentially restricts livelihoods and raises concerns about religious imposition.

articles.title: Meenakshi Natarajan, Madhya Pradesh, KC Venugopal: Rajya Sabha Pick Meenakshi Natarajan's Nomination Junked, Congress Protests
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission rejected the nomination of Meenakshi Natarajan, a Congress candidate, for the Rajya Sabha election due to her failure to disclose a pending case against her in her nomination papers.  Natarajan accused the BJP of manipulating the election and undermining democracy. The Congress protested the decision but was unsuccessful. The Election Commission has accepted a memorandum from the Congress and will seek a report from the Returning Officer, who is expected to meet with the party tomorrow.

articles.title: As logjam over Bengaluru development portfolio continues, insiders point fingers at CM Shivakumar | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Krishna Byre Gowda, the newly appointed Bengaluru development minister, has yet to assume his role five days after appointment due to confusion over the scope of his portfolio.  D K Shivakumar, the Karnataka Chief Minister, retained control over key agencies like the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) and the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority (BMRDA), sparking dissent from senior leader Ramalinga Reddy. Despite initial disagreements, Reddy has since taken charge of the irrigation ministry.  Gowda, who was in Delhi on Tuesday, has not commented on the delay.

articles.title: Amritpal Singh, Sukhbir Badal, Punar SurjitAkali Dal Rebel Manpreet Singh Ayali Joins Waris Punjab De, Boosts Party's Statewide Ambitions
articles.rephrased_article: Manpreet Singh Ayali, a former lieutenant of Sukhbir Singh Badal, has joined the Waris Punjab De party ahead of the upcoming Punjab Assembly elections. This move signifies a significant shift in state politics, deepening the crisis within the Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) and potentially eroding its Panthic base. Ayali's departure from the breakaway faction SAD (Punar Surjit) further weakens the party's legislative presence, leaving it with only one MLA, Ganieve Kaur Majithia.  The Waris Punjab De, led by Amritpal Singh, is gaining traction by addressing public concerns and positioning itself as an independent force.

articles.title: Modi is using a cannon to kill a cockroach | Narendra Modi | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government has taken action against a satirical parody account called "Cockroach Janta Party" after it gained popularity online. The Chief Justice Surya Kant made a comparison to cockroaches and parasites, which sparked the creation of the account.  The government has pressured the page to be removed from social media platforms, accusing its founder of being influenced by foreign powers. This action is seen as an overreaction to harmless satire and reflects the growing discontent among young Indians who are facing challenges such as unemployment, climate change, and a lack of trust in their government.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Government silencing dissent through pressure on social media is a serious concern.

articles.title: World Leaders Praise PM Modi As He Becomes India's Longest-Serving Prime Minister
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi etched his name into India's political history books on Tuesday, surpassing Jawaharlal Nehru's record to become the country's longest-serving elected Prime Minister.  World leaders praised his transformative domestic governance and growing influence on the global stage. Sri Lanka's President Anura Kumara Disanayaka, Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister James Marape, and Trinidad and Tobago's Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar all sent messages of congratulations, recognizing India's transformed stature under Modi's leadership.

articles.title: DSS to hold rallies on June 16 seeking Karnataka Cabinet berth for H.C. Mahadevappa - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dalit Sangharsha Samiti, a Karnataka-based organization, announced a statewide rally on June 16th to demand a Cabinet berth for H.C. Mahadevappa, a senior Congress leader and former Minister. The group highlighted Mahadevappa's contributions to Dalit welfare and social justice during his tenure as Minister, citing specific initiatives like securing funds for the Dr B.R. Ambedkar Bhavan and strengthening enforcement of laws against atrocities against Scheduled Castes. They urged the state Congress leadership to accommodate Mahadevappa in the next Cabinet expansion and provide adequate representation for Dalits in other positions of power.

articles.title: Anbumani meets T.N. CM Vijay, urges caste-based survey announcement in Governor’s address - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anbumani Ramadoss, leader of the Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK), met with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in Chennai to urge the state government to announce a caste-based survey during the Governor’s address on June 18th.  Mr. Ramadoss stated that the resolution passed at a multi-party meeting last week, which included representatives from 42 political parties and organizations, unanimously supported conducting a caste-based survey in Tamil Nadu. He argued that the existing reservation policies were based on outdated data collected during the British period and that a modern survey would provide accurate socio-economic and educational details of the state's population.

articles.title: Threats Against Politicians Skyrocketed After Meta Changed Its Speech Rules | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Meta overhauled its content moderation rules last year, claiming to relax restrictions and promote free speech.  A new report from the Center for Countering Digital Hate (CCDH) found that abusive and racist comments targeting lawmakers tripled in the six months after the changes. The report also documented a significant increase in threats against President Trump and other hateful content. While Meta maintains its decision was driven by free speech principles, experts argue that relaxing moderation has led to an amplification of harmful content, potentially contributing to increased political violence and harassment.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Increased threats against politicians signal a potential threat to democracy.

articles.title: T.N. govt. must ensure senior citizens are provided safe shelter, food, and medical care: Tamilisai Soundararajan - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan, BJP leader, expressed deep concern over the suicides of three elderly persons in Namakkal and urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to address the issue by identifying vulnerable seniors and providing them with support services.  She called for government action to ensure adequate care, including shelter, food, medical attention, and emotional assistance. Soundararajan also highlighted the importance of protecting senior citizens' dignity and well-being.

articles.title: West Bengal CID reaches Mamata Banerjee’s residence in signature forgery case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of West Bengal Police searched the residence of former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee at 30B, Harish Chatterjee Street in connection with allegations of forged signatures from party MLAs.  Subhasish Chakraborty, a former Trinamool Congress MP, prevented the search and requested a return visit when either Mamata Banerjee or Abhishek Banerjee would be present. The CID has registered an FIR based on complaints by MLAs Ritabarta Banerjee and Sandipan Saha alleging forged signatures that led to their expulsion from the party.

articles.title: Trinamool, Abhishek Banerjee offices searched in signature forgery case | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The West Bengal CID conducted searches at the Trinamool Congress's central office in Kolkata and Abhishek Banerjee's office on Camac Street as part of its investigation into alleged Assembly signature forgery.  The searches followed a complaint filed by rebel TMC MLAs Ritabrata Banerjee and Sandipan Saha alleging fabricated signatures on a letter sent to the Assembly Speaker regarding the appointment of the Leader of Opposition. The CID has recorded statements from 13 TMC MLAs, with three disowning the signatures attributed to them. Abhishek Banerjee skipped a third summons issued by the Crime Investigation Department citing pending proceedings before the Calcutta High Court and his absence from the city.

articles.title: Modi at 4,399 Days: The making of India’s longest-serving elected prime minister | The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Narendra Modi has surpassed Jawaharlal Nehru's record for the longest tenure as India's elected Prime Minister, achieving 4,399 days in office. Since assuming power in 2014, he has secured three consecutive mandates and led a period of significant economic growth and national development.  His leadership has been marked by initiatives like Swachh Bharat, Ayushman Bharat, and digital governance reforms, as well as assertive foreign policy stances that have strengthened India's global standing. The writer believes Modi is the "Man of Destiny for India" who will shape the country's future as "Swarnim Bharat."

articles.title: Rajya Sabha polls: Amid fears of cross-voting, Madhya Pradesh Congress MLAs leave for Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress MLAs in Madhya Pradesh are traveling to Bengaluru by chartered flight to avoid potential cross-voting in the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections.  The Air Traffic Control (ATC) has delayed the takeoff, causing frustration among the lawmakers.  Umang Singhar, Leader of Opposition in the state Assembly, stated that several BJP offers have been made to Congress MLAs, but they are united and confident in their support.

articles.title: Congress MLAs Stranded At Bhopal Airport Over Plane Mix-up
articles.rephrased_article: Congress MLAs and their families faced confusion at Bhopal Airport due to a smaller aircraft than expected for their travel to Bengaluru. The Congress had arranged two batches of flights, with the first flight accommodating 76 MLAs and family members, while another was planned later in the evening for the remaining MLAs.  The move came amid heightened political tension after the BJP fielded Mahesh Kevat as a candidate for the Rajya Sabha seat against Congress's Meenakshi Natarajan. The Congress is concerned about potential cross-voting and has decided to send its MLAs to Karnataka.

articles.title: BJP Leader Girish Mahajan Criticises Operation Bluestar In Big Shift In Punjab Strategy
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has shifted its Punjab strategy by publicly criticizing Operation Bluestar for the first time. Maharashtra minister Girish Mahajan, who visited the Damdami Taksal during the 42nd anniversary of the operation, described it as an attack on the Golden Temple and blamed former prime minister Indira Gandhi. This move signals an attempt to engage with Sikh sentiments that view the operation as a deep wound. However, the strategy has been met with criticism from Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, who accused the BJP of hypocrisy. Whether this outreach will be seen as reconciliation or electoral opportunism remains to be seen.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Public criticism of Operation Bluestar is a significant shift in BJP's Punjab strategy.

articles.title: Maharashtra Cabinet clears administrative restructuring, 10 new departments to be added - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Maharashtra Cabinet approved major administrative restructuring, increasing the number of departments from 33 to 43. The changes involve redistributing functions and responsibilities within existing departments to improve efficiency and decision-making.  The Cabinet also approved amendments to various Acts related to universities, taxation, and industrial development, including an ordinance for MIDC borrowing powers. These decisions were made by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis at a Cabinet meeting.

articles.title: Haunted by 2020, Congress flies Madhya Pradesh MLAs to Karnataka before Rajya Sabha vote | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: To secure a third seat in the June 18 Rajya Sabha election, the BJP needs additional votes.  The Congress has relocated nearly all of its 61 MLAs to Karnataka, citing concerns about potential BJP attempts to contact them. The move is seen as a precautionary measure to prevent defections and maintain party unity ahead of the vote.  Congress leaders have denied any discontent among their legislators and insist they are united in supporting their nominee, Meenakshi Natarajan.

articles.title: ED summons ex-Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan’s daughter T. Veena for questioning in CMRL pay-off case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned T. Veena, daughter of former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, and other officials of Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) to appear before investigators on June 12, 2026, in connection with a money-laundering case linked to the CMRL pay-off case.

articles.title: Muslim Community representatives, civil societies to establish task force to tackle hate crimes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Maulana Ilyas Khan, president of Jamaat-e-Islami Maharashtra, announced the formation of a task force to provide aid to victims of hate crimes. The announcement came after a meeting organized by the Federation of Maharashtra Muslims (FMM), which also included representatives from the Justice and Peace Commission (JPC), Institute for Community Research Organisation (ICOR), and other civil societies.  The meeting aimed to address concerns about anti-conversion laws, the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), and rising communal tensions in the state.

articles.title: Congress on reduction in number of subsidised Ujjwala refills - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress criticized the government's reduction of subsidized LPG refills under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, accusing it of "crocodile tears" and prioritizing power over poverty alleviation.  Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge highlighted the program's dwindling benefits, from 12 subsidized refills to just 4, while criticizing the government for increasing LPG prices despite claiming affordability. The Government, however, defended its actions, stating that Indian households still pay among the lowest global cooking gas prices despite international price hikes.

articles.title: Beyond Religion, Caste, Class: BJP Eyes UP Via Madhya Pradesh Rajya Sabha Seat
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP has nominated Mahesh Kewat, chairman of the Madhya Pradesh State Fisherman Welfare Board, to represent the state in the Rajya Sabha. This nomination is being interpreted as a symbolic gesture drawing on the Ramayana story of Lord Ram's boatman, Kewat, who helped him cross the river.
